source: pi-platform-spec Book 2 Part 7.4; the quick ideas are rewritten with the owner's approval (owner_rewrites.json), so they are not verbatim

ideas: Ask staff to message a photo of any shelf running low to one shared chat, so the buyer sees it straight away.
Check the expiry dates on the oldest stock first and move it to the front, so nothing is left to expire at the back.
Move slow items to the front with a small offer before buying more, so shelf space goes to what actually sells.
Send a photo of each transfer note in a shared chat before the goods leave, so a missing parcel is spotted quickly.

dropped.text: count the 20 best-selling items every evening instead of everything once a month
dropped.why: a number, percentage, amount or promised result (no invented claims)

stock_inventory.never_say: "you'll never run out again", any shrinkage percentage

ideas: Compare each shop's sales with the shop that sells best, so you can see where the drop is happening.
Ask staff to note why browsing customers left without buying, so you learn what stops the sale.
Try one offer on your slowest day and compare it with a normal one, so you see if it brings people in.

dropped.text: find the 10 items that sell most and make sure they're always on display
dropped.why: a number, percentage, amount or promised result (no invented claims)

ideas: Count the cash at closing with two people and post the total in one shared chat, so a gap is seen at once.
Keep one shared list of who owes you and send a polite WhatsApp reminder, so nobody is forgotten.
Deposit the cash at the same fixed time every time, so it never sits around the shop.
For cash on delivery, check each courier's statement against your orders, so missing payments show up.
cash_collections.never_say: anything about loans, financing, interest or tax treatment RADV

ideas: Write down what each of your best-selling items costs you and what it sells for, so you can see which ones really earn.
Add delivery, packing and marketplace fees to what each item costs you before you decide what to charge, so no cost is forgotten.
Ask each supplier for the same item in writing and compare the offers side by side, so you see who is dearer.
margin_cost.never_say: what price they should charge; tax advice

ideas: Collect every customer's WhatsApp number at billing, with their permission, so you can reach them again.
Message the past customers who agreed to hear from you when new stock arrives, so they come back first.
Reply politely to every review, good or bad, so new customers see that you listen.

dropped.text: ask "how did you hear about us?" at the counter
dropped.why: a question inside an idea (R-ASK: the one question is pi's last sentence)

customers_retention.never_say: "customers will come back"; anything that sends messages without customers' permission

ideas: Complete the online map listing of every location with photos, timings and a WhatsApp number, so people find you and can ask you easily.
Put a code or a "show this message" offer in every ad, so you can tell which ad brings people.
Reply to every enquiry quickly, even with just "we'll send details shortly", so people do not go to the next shop.
Stop the ads that bring no visits or enquiries after a fair test, so the money goes to the ones that work.

dropped.text: post new arrivals with prices on WhatsApp Status and Instagram
dropped.why: money or a regulated topic: a person decides

marketing_leads.never_say: cost-per-lead numbers, "go viral", platform policy advice

ideas: Move every order from the different chats into one shared list, so none is missed or taken twice.
Confirm cash on delivery orders on WhatsApp before dispatch, so fewer parcels come back refused.
Tell customers their delivery day upfront, so they are not left guessing.
Note the reason for every return in one place, so you see what keeps going wrong.
Keep open purchase orders in one shared list and message the supplier before the expected date, so a late delivery shows early.
Check quality when goods arrive and send a photo of any problem to the supplier, so it is fixed before you pay.
Buy based on what sold well recently, not on what the order booker pushes, so money is not tied up in slow stock.
Put the shift schedule in the staff chat well ahead, so everyone knows when they work.
Ask staff to send a photo after each opening and closing check, so you can see it was done.
Share a target with each shop and the result in the team chat, so everyone sees how they are doing.
Have new staff shadow your best person at first, so they learn the right way from the start.
people_staff.never_say: labour-law or termination advice; anything about watching staff without their knowledge

ideas: Write the most repeated tasks as simple steps and share them in the staff chat, so anyone can do them the same way.
Find the task you type twice and pick one place for it, so you only enter it once.
Set one person responsible for each recurring job, so nothing is left for someone else to do.
Keep a maintenance log for key machines in a shared note, so a problem is caught before it stops work.
Have each shop send its key numbers in one format at a fixed time, so you can compare the shops easily.
Compare each shop's numbers with the best shop, so you see where to look first.

dropped.why: more than one sentence (R-VAL-03); a number, percentage, amount or promised result (no invented claims)

ideas: List every tool you use and what you type into it, so you see where the same thing is typed twice.
Pick one place to be the main record, so there is one version to trust.

dropped.text: back up your Excel or register photos weekly
dropped.why: how-to, steps, settings or wording to copy (R-VAL-04, R-VAL-05); names a vendor, an app to buy, a product or a competitor

ideas: Check a sample of every batch or job before it leaves, so a fault is caught before the customer sees it.
Note each complaint with a photo and the reason, so you can see what keeps repeating.
Share the top complaint with the team, so everyone works on the same fix.
Keep documents in one shared folder by month on your phone, so nothing is hunted for later.

dropped.text: keep a calendar of every licence, renewal and filing date
dropped.why: money or a regulated topic: a person decides

compliance_admin.never_say: what the law requires, tax amounts, filing advice

ideas: Use one group per purpose instead of one group for everything, so important messages are not lost.
Close the working day with a short "what's pending" message in the team chat, so nothing is forgotten.
Give every task one owner and a date, so everyone knows who is doing it and by when.
Have two people at cash and stock counts, so a mistake or a loss is seen by someone else too.
Check the voids and refunds regularly, so odd ones are noticed early.
Count high-value items more often than the rest, so a missing one shows up early.
loss_security.never_say: accusations, legal action advice, covert monitoring

ideas: Look at last season's sales by week to plan stock, so you buy for the busy and slow periods.
Open a new branch only after the current branch's numbers are clear, so the next one rests on facts.
Add online booking or ordering if most enquiries ask the same thing, so customers can do it themselves.
Fix the website's contact button first, so interested people can reach you easily.
